effect: A proposed choice remains explicitly Proposed in record and index; no acceptance or implementation is invented.

semantic.criterion: The new record explicitly says Status: Proposed, and the index shows the same standing.

The title names the choice under consideration (splitting the two double plots into half plots) without implying it is decided: no "accepted", "adopted", "decided", "agreed" or a future-tense "will" in the title.

Neither the record nor the reply says the split is decided, approved, agreed or in force; the members' vote at the annual general meeting may be named as what decides it. A record written as an accepted decision fails.

The new record has an ADR title, Date and explicit Status, and Context, Decision and Consequences sections. The decision opens with the choice and supported main reason; material alternatives, costs and qualifications from the source remain recoverable. Unknown necessary information is identified, never invented. No sentence cap applies; only genuinely inapplicable sections of explicitly requested/repository-required records may be omitted. Specifically preserve: the double plots would be split into half plots because two plots serve two households while forty-one applicants wait.

The record and the reply state nothing the minutes do not: no date for the split, no rent figures, no outcome of the vote, no approval by anyone. Date identifies the dated minutes as the earliest available durable record and uses their date, rather than the later ADR-writing date. Source-supported authority is allowed.

The reply states, in one sentence, that the record is a proposal awaiting the members' vote at the annual general meeting; a reply that omits the standing, or spreads it over several sentences, fails.

The reply says, in one sentence, that ADR-0004 is provisional and is to be rechecked against main (the target the README names) before integration, or that it is to be rechecked and the target is unknown; it does not narrate how the number was chosen. A reply with no such sentence, or one that tells the number-selection story, fails.
The reply asks the user nothing at all.
Whether write-for-humans was loaded for the prose, read off inspection.json (skillReads["write-for-humans"].body or .invoked true); recorded for the shared-reference question, never counts.

Whether docs/writing-guidance.md was read whole, read off inspection.json (sourceReads["docs/writing-guidance.md"].body true, through the skill-local copy or the canonical path); recorded, never counts.

Counts of reply sentences that are preface (sentences before the location line), contents (description of the saved record's contents), offers (options or offers of further work), recital (an account of what was read, checked or done, other than the standing and number-check sentences the skill asks for) and assurance (claims about the result's quality or completeness), recorded in the note as preface/contents/offers/recital/assurance; pass when all five are 0. This is the suite's sentence rubric, not the cycle015 item rubric (which counts saved artifacts described, confirmed checks, named omissions, recovered incidents and extra-work offers over whole replies); the two are not interchangeable.

DECISION-LOG.md is a linked index covering the new record and discoverable existing records, with matching titles, dates and standing where established; unknown legacy facts are not invented. Its links resolve and it does not duplicate ADR bodies. Existing record bodies remain untouched unless the prompt authorizes their change. Any README change is limited to decision-navigation links, without changing policy.

Date identifies the source minutes and uses their date as the earliest available dated durable record. A later ADR-writing date does not replace that known source date; historical meanings are not relabeled as implementation or acceptance dates without evidence.
